stem: A child still has marked out-toeing beyond the usual time of spontaneous resolution; which concern is specifically linked to the need for intervention?
explanation: Patellofemoral pain is the concern linked to persistent out-toeing and may justify intervention if the condition does not resolve spontaneously.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because proximal muscle weakness is not the concern specifically associated with persistent out-toeing.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because persistent out-toeing is associated with a risk of patellofemoral pain, which is a reason intervention may be needed if it does not resolve.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because dysmorphism is not the reason for intervention in persistent out-toeing.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because retinal abnormalities are not linked to persistent out-toeing.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because head lag relates to infant motor assessment, not persistent out-toeing.
